# Shared protocol conformance corpus.
#
# Gate C requires that "a host simulator or protocol fixture and the firmware
# agree on framing and versions". This file is that agreement, written down.
# Two independent implementations of the same draft agree right up until they do
# not; a corpus both must reproduce is what turns that into a test failure
# instead of a bring-up surprise.
#
# Consumed by:
#   - pycontrol/tests/test_fixture_corpus.py   (the Python simulator)
#   - test/native/test_protocol/test_protocol.cpp             (the RP2040 half)
#
# BOTH consumers exist as of 2026-09-03, which is when this file started being
# evidence rather than a restatement of one implementation. Change a case and
# BOTH must be re-run: `pixi run pycontrol-test` and `pixi run -- pio test -e
# native`. A change that only one side is checked against silently forks the
# contract.
#
# Format is line-oriented, not JSON, so the C++ side can parse it with getline
# and a prefix compare rather than pulling in a JSON library. It is also
# diffable and greppable, which is the same rule the protocol itself follows.
#
#   CASE <name>       begin a case; the board is freshly booted, READY drained,
#                     clock at 0, serial 0000000000000000, defaults otherwise
#   SEND <line>       feed one command line (the \n is implied)
#   ADVANCE <us>      advance simulated time by <us> microseconds
#   EXPECT <line>     the next output line, in order
#   END               end of case; no further output may be pending
#
# Every EXPECT is exact bytes. Blank lines and # lines are ignored.
#
# Board defaults these cases assume, from BoardSim's constructor:
#   serial 0000000000000000   fw 0.0.0   hw rev0   proto 1   axes 1
#   travel -20.0..20.0 deg    v_max 180.0 deg/s    home takes 50000 us
#   host timeout 100000 us
#
# Move distances here are chosen to divide evenly at v_max (9 deg = 50000 us) so
# no case depends on how a duration is rounded. The firmware and the simulator
# both truncate, but that is not something a corpus should be pinning by
# accident - if rounding ever matters, it needs a case that says so on purpose.


# --------------------------------------------------------------- versions

# The one case that must never be allowed to drift silently: a peer reads the
# protocol version and axis count from here and refuses a mismatch rather than
# guessing. The axis count is also what distinguishes this board from the
# twin-axis board on the same link.
CASE id-reports-version-serial-and-axis-count
  SEND id;1
  EXPECT ack;1;hw=rev0;serial=0000000000000000;fw=0.0.0;proto=1;axes=1;caps=motion+home+freewheel+instr+hv;rxbuf=120
END

# "Must work before ARM and must never fail" - including before HV is on.
CASE id-answers-before-arm
  SEND id;7
  EXPECT ack;7;hw=rev0;serial=0000000000000000;fw=0.0.0;proto=1;axes=1;caps=motion+home+freewheel+instr+hv;rxbuf=120
END


# ------------------------------------------------ the draft's own examples

# `cal;419;get -> ack;419;enc_offset=1024;angle_zero=0.0`
CASE draft-example-cal-get
  SEND cal;419;get
  EXPECT ack;419;enc_offset=1024;angle_zero=0.0
END

# `movetoo;420;-12.5 -> nak;420;badverb`
CASE draft-example-unknown-verb
  SEND movetoo;420;-12.5
  EXPECT nak;420;badverb
END

# `moveto;421;-999 -> nak;421;outofrange`
#
# The draft shows this reply without saying which state the board was in, and
# ordering matters: this implementation checks ARMED *before* range, so from a
# fresh board the same line answers `notarmed`. Reproducing the draft's example
# therefore requires an armed board, which is what this case sets up. The
# ordering choice is deliberate - refusing motion outside ARMED is the
# safety-relevant rule and should not be reachable past an argument check.
CASE draft-example-out-of-range-when-armed
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND moveto;421;-999
  EXPECT nak;421;outofrange
END


# ------------------------------------------------------ framing robustness

CASE bad-frame-without-a-sequence-number
  SEND ping
  EXPECT nak;?;badframe
END

CASE bad-frame-with-an-unreadable-sequence-number
  SEND ping;notanumber
  EXPECT nak;?;badframe
END

CASE empty-field-is-a-bad-frame
  SEND ;
  EXPECT nak;?;badframe
END

# Verbs decode case-insensitively; the draft's table is uppercase and its
# examples are lowercase.
CASE verbs-are-case-insensitive
  SEND PING;3
  EXPECT ack;3
END

# A CRLF peer leaves a carriage return before the newline.
CASE carriage-return-is-tolerated
  SEND ping;4\r
  EXPECT ack;4
END

# A repeated seq with identical content is re-acknowledged, byte for byte.
CASE retransmission-is-reacknowledged-identically
  SEND cal;9;set;enc_offset;2048
  EXPECT ack;9;enc_offset=2048
  SEND cal;9;set;enc_offset;2048
  EXPECT ack;9;enc_offset=2048
END


# ------------------------------------------------------- state machine gates

CASE motion-is-refused-outside-armed
  SEND moveto;1;5.0
  EXPECT nak;1;notarmed
END

# The ordering above is pinned deliberately: ARMED is checked BEFORE the range
# check, so an OUT-OF-RANGE value from an UNARMED board answers `notarmed` and
# not `outofrange`. Refusing motion outside ARMED is the safety-relevant rule
# and must not be reachable past an argument check.
#
# `motion-is-refused-outside-armed` above cannot pin this, because 5.0 is in
# range and both orderings answer `notarmed`. Only an out-of-range value from an
# unarmed board tells the two apart. Added 2026-09-03 after mutation-testing the
# corpus against the firmware: inverting the two checks passed every case in
# this file, which meant the corpus documented an ordering it did not enforce.
CASE armed-is-checked-before-the-range-check
  SEND moveto;1;-999
  EXPECT nak;1;notarmed
END

CASE homing-requires-the-motor-rail
  SEND home;1
  EXPECT nak;1;nohv
END

CASE arm-is-refused-before-homing
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND arm;2
  EXPECT nak;2;nothomed
END

# The full path from boot to a completed move, which is the sequence a task
# actually performs.
CASE arm-then-move-to-completion
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND moveto;4;9.0
  EXPECT ack;4
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;TARGET;100000;angle=9.0
END

# Heartbeat loss faults the board without host cooperation, drops HV_EN, and is
# reported as fault bit 0.
CASE heartbeat-loss-faults-the-board
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  ADVANCE 100000
  EXPECT ev;FAULT;150000;code=0;detail=host_timeout
  SEND status;4
  EXPECT ack;4;state=FAULTED;angle=0.0;xactual=0.0;homed=1;limit=0;faults=1;hv=0
END


# ------------------------------------------------------------- observability

CASE status-is-safe-before-anything-is-configured
  SEND status;1
  EXPECT ack;1;state=IDLE;angle=0.0;xactual=0.0;homed=0;limit=0;faults=0;hv=0
END

CASE limits-reports-what-the-board-will-enforce
  SEND limits;1
  EXPECT ack;1;travel_lo=-20.0;travel_hi=20.0;v_max=180.0;a_max=3600.0;i_max=0.421
END

CASE hv-state-is-observable-not-inferred
  SEND hv;1;state
  EXPECT ack;1;hv=0
  SEND hv;2;on
  EXPECT ack;2
  SEND hv;3;state
  EXPECT ack;3;hv=1
END


# ------------------------------------------------------------- compliance

# The trial shape the rig actually needs: park, present, then let the animal
# move the joystick.
#
# Rev 0 has no electronic brake, so `freewheel` is its own verb. On a board with
# the brake it must not be: the brake has to engage BEFORE motor drive is
# released, and two host commands cannot guarantee that ordering across a link
# with latency. This case is expected to be REPLACED by a `brake` case, not
# extended.
CASE freewheel-releases-the-driver
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND freewheel;4
  EXPECT ack;4
  SEND status;5
  EXPECT ack;5;state=FREEWHEEL;angle=0.0;xactual=0.0;homed=1;limit=0;faults=0;hv=1
END

# Freewheeling is only reachable from ARMED. A joystick held by an energised
# motor cannot go compliant by accident.
CASE freewheel-is-refused-before-arming
  SEND freewheel;1
  EXPECT nak;1;notarmed
END

# Moving to a bounded position is what presents the joystick to the animal.
CASE move-to-the-pull-position
  SEND hv;1;on
  EXPECT ack;1
  SEND home;2
  EXPECT ack;2
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;HOMED;50000;angle=0.0
  SEND arm;3
  EXPECT ack;3
  SEND moveto;4;-9.0
  EXPECT ack;4
  ADVANCE 50000
  EXPECT ev;TARGET;100000;angle=-9.0
END
